note: Stated sizes, distances, counts and bearings, chapter by chapter, as the researchers recorded them. The narrative half is DIMENSIONS.md; this is the half a script can read. Written by scripts/coverage_merge.py.

XII.what: which hand carries the torch, and which hand takes Poliphilo's
XII.book_says: The most fayre Nymph beeing come to Poliphilus, bearing a Torch in her left hand, with the other tooke him and inuited him to walke with her
XII.source: Dallington p. 206-207 (1499 p. 147) -- direction/handedness, not a distance; the only quantifiable or orientational detail anywhere in this chapter's six pages

XIV.what: triumphal car body length, in plan ("two perfect squares")
XIV.book_says: of two perfect squares in length, of six feet

XIV.what: triumphal car body width and height
XIV.book_says: three high and as much wide

XIV.what: height of the flat deck above the plinth cornice
XIV.book_says: from here upward, a foot and a half, there was a flat

XIV.what: width of the flat deck (where the rider stands/sits)
XIV.book_says: a flat two feet and a half wide

XIV.what: length of the flat deck
XIV.book_says: five and a half long, with a slope towards the cornice

XIV.what: height of the topaz censer-vessels carried by the two riders nearest each car
XIV.book_says: of two feet in height, without handles, of a wonderful artifice

XIV.what: beasts drawing each of the four triumphal cars
XIV.book_says: six wanton centaurs / six white elephants / six...unicorns / six spotted tigers

XIV.what: nymph riders on each car -- but only three of the four cars
XIV.book_says: Each was ridden by a notable Nymph (six per car, cars 1-3); the fourth car's team description has no rider sentence at all

XIV.what: orientation of the six riders on a car, left/right
XIV.book_says: three with their notable faces turned to the right, and three to the left

XIV.what: diameter and height of the urn's gold base
XIV.book_says: a base of gold, of a lowest diameter of one foot and three palms, and of nearly the same height

XIV.what: height of the main jacinth vessel
XIV.book_says: In height it was two feet and a half

XIV.what: diameter (thickness) of the main jacinth vessel
XIV.book_says: The diameter of its thickness stood at a foot and a half

XIV.what: circumference of the main jacinth vessel, as the book itself derives it
XIV.book_says: the circumference was three diameters

XIV.what: cumulative height from the base to where the ewer-shaped neck begins
XIV.book_says: in all, as far as here, it is a foot and a half

XIV.what: thickness of the border at the base of the ewer-neck
XIV.book_says: there was a border going round the last thickness of a palm... a palm

XIV.what: further rise of the vessel's form above the border
XIV.book_says: there grew a form of the vessel aforesaid, raised a foot

XIV.what: further widening of the neck above that rise
XIV.book_says: began to widen for a palm and a half

XIV.what: diameter at the widened neck -- unit uncertain, see caveat
XIV.book_says: The diameter two quarters and a half [CAVEAT: 'quarter' is not in DIMENSIONS.md's unit table; read here as a quarter of a Roman foot -- 4 palms to a foot, so 1 quarter = 1 palm = 0.074 m -- giving 2.5 x 0.074, an interpretation and not a settled conversion]

XIV.what: rise from the widened neck to the vessel's mouth -- same uncertain unit
XIV.book_says: Then it rose most beautifully to the mouth two quarters and a half

XIV.what: the carved girding/leafy band around the vessel's waist
XIV.book_says: a girding band of two feet

XIV.what: the plain space to each side, beneath the girding band
XIV.book_says: the space that stands a foot and a half to each side

XIV.what: height of each of the four corner candelabra
XIV.book_says: with a notable display, adorned with fine-wrought work, of a height of two feet

XIV.what: number of candelabra, one to each corner of the car's flat
XIV.book_says: At each corner of the flat of the triumphal car there shone widely, set there, a most skilfully made candelabrum

XXII.what: Theatre Area, diameter
XXII.book_says: 32 paces (p. 351)

XXII.what: Theatre's built ring (colonnade) around the Area, thickness
XXII.book_says: 8 paces (p. 351)

XXII.what: Seat-box height
XXII.book_says: 6 palms (p. 353)

XXII.what: Seat-box depth (opening)
Walkway at each pergola tier
XXII.book_says: 5 feet wide (p. 353)

XXII.what: Pergola height over each walkway
XXII.book_says: 1 1/2 pace high (p. 353)

XXII.what: Spacing between paired crowning cypresses
XXII.book_says: 3 paces distant (p. 354)

XXII.what: The clean band above the royal cornice (not yet in DIMENSIONS.md)
XXII.book_says: a pace and a half high (p. 350)

XXII.what: The trough within the topmost gallery wall, capacity at bottom and opening alike (not yet in DIMENSIONS.md)
XXII.book_says: a pace and a half, inclusive (p. 354)

XXII.what: The embroidered band round Cupid's triumphal car (not yet in DIMENSIONS.md; a 'dodrans' is not in DIMENSIONS.md section 1's unit table -- computed here as 3/4 Roman foot, the standard Latin sense of dodrans)
XXII.book_says: a dodrans wide (p. 341)

XXII.what: Psyche's shoulder-diamond, length -- UNIT WARNING: 'inch' and 'thumb' are not in DIMENSIONS.md section 1's table at all (only foot/palm/cubit/pace/stadium/mile are). Computed here as a rough guess at a Roman uncia (1/12 foot = 0.0247 m); not verified against any project reference and should not be trusted at the same confidence as the pace/foot/palm figures above
XXII.book_says: an inch-and-a-half long lengthwise, a thumb in breadth (p. 341)

XXII.what: Theatre's colonnade plan: quadrants x bays per quadrant (a count, not a length)
XXII.book_says: quadrifariously divided [4 quarters], eight divisions [bays] apiece = 32 bays total (p. 351)

XXII.what: Number of column orders, and the rule they break (a count/proportion, not a length)
XXII.book_says: three orders, kept at one height, against the Vitruvian rule that each upper order be a quarter shorter (a fifth, for the third) (p. 350)

XXII.what: Number of planted tiers in the cavea (a count, not a length)
XXII.book_says: four hollow steps to an order, three orders = twelve planted tiers total (pp. 353-354)

XXII.what: The stair opposite the entrance door (a count and a direction)
XXII.book_says: 'in prospect of the door of our entrance' [i.e. directly opposite it], a stair of seven steps (p. 356)

XXII.what: The two gem-vases flanking the golden gate (a count and a direction)
XXII.book_says: 'one to a side': one of sapphire, the other of emerald (p. 347)

XXII.what: Greek letters impressed on Capnolina's smoking vase (a count)
XXII.book_says: thirteen most-measured Greek letters -- ΠΑΝΤΑ ΒΑΙΑ ΒΙΟΥ (13 characters) (p. 340)

XXII.what: Named female figures individually described across the chapter's masque (a count)
XXII.book_says: at least 19: Imeria, Erototimoris, Toxodora, Ennia, Phileda, Velode, Omonia, Diapraxe, Typhlote, Asynecha, Ardelia Comazista, Aschemosyne, Teleste, Vrachivia, Capnolina, Synesia, Plexaura, Ganoma, Psyche (pp. 338-344)

XXII.what: Named or individually-described trophies/standards preceding the car (a count)
XXII.book_says: at least seven: the Mars/Pyroeis trophy, the Jupiter trophy, the Hercules trophy, QUIS EVADET, NEMO, the crescent-crown trophy, the DORYKTETOI lead standard -- plus 'many others, of prolix telling' left uncounted (pp. 326-330)

XXII.what: Aegipans in the rear file (a count)
XXII.book_says: two aegipans, an unspecified further number of satyrs (p. 344)

XXIII.what: height of the fountain's kerb (the 'little wall' at its centre)
XXIII.book_says: there rose at its centre a little wall a foot high

XXIII.what: height of the seven columns, from the golden bases to the architrave
XXIII.book_says: from the golden bases up to the architrave the height stood at seven feet

XXIII.what: length of each face of the heptagonal kerb/arcade (where the inscription is cut, three letters to a face)
depth/height of the cut Greek lettering on the columns
XXIII.book_says: letters of the most ancient Greek, the shaft being three-quarters of a foot
XXIII.source: p. 361 (translator flags this clause as compressed/uncertain -- may describe the letters' cutting depth rather than height; check against facsimile)

XXIII.what: height of each gold planetary figure on the crown
XXIII.book_says: an image of a planet with its proper attribute... its size exactly a third of the column below it
XXIII.source: p. 360 (derived: one third of the 7-foot/2.072 m column height given on p. 361)

XXIII.what: number of gem columns, and of the planetary figures above them
XXIII.book_says: seven of them in all, turned with the utmost exquisiteness

XXIII.what: number of zodiac signs carved in the frieze beneath the planetary altars
XXIII.book_says: in the frieze running round... were to be seen the twelve signs of the zodiac

XXIII.what: number of steps down from the topmost step (where the columns stand) to the fountain's lip
XXIII.book_says: six little steps more went down to the lip of the fountain, of dark agate

XXIII.what: how high the fountain's water stands, relative to the six steps
XXIII.book_says: The fountain's water reached to the edge of the fourth step; the others stood clear of it
XXIII.source: p. 363 (relative level, not a stated absolute distance)

XXIII.what: number of nymphs Venus first assigns to attend Polia and Poliphilo at the rite
XXIII.book_says: she assigned three apiece to Polia and to him

XXIII.what: number of nymphs Venus assigns afterward as lifelong companions
XXIII.book_says: I will give and consign to you four illustrious little maidens... likewise I present four other noble and most accomplished maidens into your unceasing company

XXIII.what: number of letters in the fountain's motto as Colonna states the layout
XXIII.book_says: On the front face only two letters were to be seen... and then following, on the other faces, three and three
XXIII.source: p. 361 (count: 2 + 3×6 = 20; the translator flags that the phrase ΩΣΠΕΡ ΣΠΙΝΘΗΡ ΚΗΛΗΘΜΟΣ has more than 20 letters, so the arithmetic given does not close)

XXIII.what: which columns stand where relative to the entrance, and where the curtain hangs
XXIII.book_says: Two of these stood answering one another, equally, opposite the entrance... on the right hand [sapphire]... on the left [emerald]... between the sapphire and the emerald column, hung... the most beautiful little veiling curtain

XXV.what: the children of Lelio Syliro and Trivisia Calardia Pia
XXV.book_says: "they had most-noble seed, and copious birth, taking up (bearing) more sons, male and female, alternately" -- five sons named (Maurio, Halcyoneo, Tipula, Narbonio, Musilistre) and six daughters named (Murgania, Quintia, Septimia, Alimbrica, Astorgia, Melmia)
XXV.note: A count (11 = 5 + 6), not a distance; included per the recipe's instruction to log stated counts. No unit conversion applies.

XV.what: height of the juniper-and-box hedge enclosing the square orchard where the Vertumnus/Pomona procession circles the altar
XV.book_says: a quick-set vpon either sides, in height one pace, of pricking iuniper thicke set togither, and mixt with box

XXXIV.what: how many letters Poliphilo has now sent Polia

XXXV.what: presences Poliphilo beholds at the throne
XXXV.book_says: three presences -- two divine, the third a little less than celestial

XXXV.what: gods named as susceptible to Venus's voice
XXXV.book_says: Mars, Jove, Saturn, Phoebus, Mercury, Diana -- six named

XXXV.what: zodiacal figures named as excluded from Venus's throne
XXXV.book_says: Virgin Astraea, Orion, the hirsute Ram -- three named

XXXVIII.what: the date of the dream, given by the closing colophon
XXXVIII.book_says: "At Treviso, where wretched Poliphilo was held fast in the most comely little thongs of Polia's love. 1467, on the Kalends of May." -- i.e. Treviso, 1 May 1467.

No clock hour is given. Poliphilo wakes "into the small hours" ("sighing, risen and released from the sweet sleep, I woke of a sudden into the small hours"), and Philomela is already singing "before daybreak" -- so the waking falls in the pre-dawn hours of 1 May, just before the sunrise the chapter goes on to describe.
